title: Officer who shot Toronto hostage-taker cleared
article: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has cleared the Toronto police sharpshooter who shot and killed a man who took a passerby hostage in front of Union Station last month.
In a ruling released Friday, the unit said the officer "had no alternative" but to fire at Sugston Anthony Brookes, 45.

Brookes died from a single shot to his head as he held a young bank employee hostage and fended off rescuers with a sawed-off rifle. After the incident, police discovered Brookes' weapon could not have harmed his hostage because it was jammed.
Before grabbing the young woman in front of Toronto's busiest commuter station, the man had fired two shots at his estranged wife outside her place of work, then beat her with the butt of his rifle.
Cornered while trying to escape, Brookes took the other woman hostage and held her by the neck for 40 minutes while police tried to negotiate her release.

The Special Investigations Unit says it interviewed dozens of police and civilian witnesses and examined both surveillance and media videotape before concluding the sharpshooter's actions were "legally justified."

Investigators also examined an undated audiotape Brookes made before the hostage-taking incident. In the tape, he said he had "made a decision," but he did not record specifically what he was planning to do or what that decision was.
The Special Investigations Unit is called in to investigate any incident in which a citizen is injured or killed as a result of police action.
